entities.summary: The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) was a pivotal entity in the arc of world history, shaped by the Cold War and emerging nationalism. Founded by Gamal Abdel Nasser in 1955 CE, NAM aimed to forge an alternative to the bipolar world order, uniting nations with diverse ideological perspectives and economic systems. This movement influenced the development of Third World nationalism, promoted economic cooperation, and challenged the dominance of the Western Bloc. The NAM played a significant role in shaping the post-colonial era, fostering a sense of global solidarity among nations, and contributing to the rise of anti-imperialism. The movement's impact can be seen in the formation of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), the Group of 77, and the Non-Aligned Movement's own successor organizations. Notably, NAM's rejection of the New International Economic Order (NIEO) and its emphasis on economic self-reliance paved the way for the emergence of the BRICS nations and the G20. As a testament to its enduring legacy, NAM's principles continue to inspire global cooperation and economic development initiatives. The NAM's significance can be quantified in the fact that it brought together 25 nations in 1961, creating a powerful counterbalance to the Western Bloc's influence. This movement's impact on global politics, economics, and international relations remains a subject of ongoing scholarly debate and analysis.
